rulings.reason: The instruction is gated on subject matter: an entry cannot score above 0 unless it is about a taboo/transgressive topic, so a high score is first evidence that the entrant picked a gross-out target rather than evidence about how well the joke works. The sensory-specificity requirement layered on top is a real descriptive-craft skill that plausibly produces better writing independent of topic, so it is mixed.

Scoring turns on naming a currently contested political figure or event, which is a topic-and-temporal marker: the same craft applied to a non-political prompt scores 0, so a high score reports what the entry is about and when it was written, not how good it is. The secondary requirement of a blunt, unhedged stance may co-occur with fully committed writing, so it is mixed.

This is a pure thematic bucket detector: it asks only whether the content is about sequels/franchise over-extension and contains no clause that evaluates execution, timing, or surprise within that theme, so a well-made and a hackneyed sequel joke score identically at 10. Because nothing in the instruction rewards quality, its upstream cause is topic selection alone and I see no plausible genuine-quality component to preserve.

The criterion scores whether the stored text happens to be truncated, which is a fingerprint of how the item was captured and stored rather than of the entrant's craft; no part of the instruction inspects wit, aptness, or construction. The proposer's own evidence shows truncated items on both the dense-high and card-high sides, so completeness does not track quality even directionally and does not warrant a mixed flag.
